subproblems.title: Top-degree currents as scalar functionals on C_c^∞ (Step 1 of Simon 2.34)
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ an arbitrary set and T ∈ D_n(U) (Lean: T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), a linear functional on the test n-forms Dⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U (m + 1) satisfying the continuity axiom GeometricCurrentOn.continuous': T(ω_k) → 0 whenever ω_k → 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges). Call b : ℝⁿ → ℝ admissible if b is C^∞, has compact support and spt b ⊆ U (spt g denotes the closed support of g, the closure of {g ≠ 0}; Lean: tsupport g). Let e = (e_1,…,e_n) be the standard basis of ℝⁿ (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1). Then there is a function u : (ℝⁿ → ℝ) → ℝ such that: (i) T(ω) = u(x ↦ ω(x)(e_1,…,e_n)) for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U); (ii) for every admissible b there is ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with ω(x)(e_1,…,e_n) = b(x) for all x ∈ ℝⁿ; (iii) u(a + b) = u(a) + u(b) for all admissible a, b; (iv) u(c·a) = c·u(a) for all c ∈ ℝ and admissible a; (v) whenever K ⊆ U is compact, a_k (k ∈ ℕ) and b are C^∞ functions ℝⁿ → ℝ with spt a_k ⊆ K for all k and spt b ⊆ K, and for every q ∈ ℕ, D^q a_k → D^q b uniformly on ℝⁿ, then u(a_k) → u(b).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 6, Theorem 2.34 (Constancy Theorem) and its printed proof, pp. 142–143, as expanded in the accepted proof of the parent node root.constancy-a1.local_on_balls-a1 (book n = m + 1; erratum applied there: the garbled printed display (1) reads T(a_ε dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ) = ∫ a θ_ε dLⁿ for a ∈ L¹(B_ρ(x₀)), with a_ε = ϕ_ε ∗ a). This child is Step 1, items (1a)–(1e), of that proof: every top-degree form is a·dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ, and T(ω) = u(a_ω) with u(a) = T(a dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ) and a_ω(x) = ω(x)(e).
Notation. n := m + 1; ℝⁿ = Eucl n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 is the i-th standard basis vector and e = (e_1,…,e_n); spt g = tsupport g (closure of {g ≠ 0}); D^q g = iteratedFDeriv ℝ q g; “C^∞” means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞). Λⁿ(ℝⁿ) = Covector (Eucl n) n is the space of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝⁿ, and Dⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n consists of the C^∞ maps ω : ℝⁿ → Λⁿ(ℝⁿ) with compact support and spt ω ⊆ U. T : Dⁿ(U) → ℝ is linear (T.toCurrent is a linear map) and satisfies the continuity axiom GeometricCurrentOn.continuous': T(ω_k) → 0 whenever ω_k → 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges, i.e. there is a compact K ⊆ U with spt ω_k ⊆ K for all k (and spt 0 ⊆ K) and, for every q, D^q ω_k → D^q 0 = 0 uniformly on K. A function b : ℝⁿ → ℝ is called admissible if b is C^∞, has compact support and spt b ⊆ U. No hypothesis on U is used.

Proof.

1. (The n-covector dx.) Let dx := dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ be the n-covector v = (v_1,…,v_n) ↦ det[(v_j)_i]_{i,j}, the determinant of the n×n matrix whose (i, j) entry is the i-th coordinate of v_j. It is the wedge product of the n coordinate functionals x ↦ x_i, hence a continuous alternating n-linear form: dx ∈ Λⁿ(ℝⁿ). The coordinate matrix of e is the identity matrix, so dx(e) = det I = 1. Every α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝⁿ) satisfies α = α(e)·dx: the alternating n-linear forms on the n-dimensional space ℝⁿ are the scalar multiples of the determinant with respect to the basis e, namely α = α(e)·det_e (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, for the basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ whose i-th vector is e_i), and det_e(v) is the determinant of the coordinate matrix of v, i.e. det_e(v) = dx(v); two continuous alternating maps that agree at every v are equal.

2. (The forms [b].) For b : ℝⁿ → ℝ put [b](x) := b(x)·dx. Let Λ : ℝ → Λⁿ(ℝⁿ), t ↦ t·dx; Λ is continuous linear, Λ(0) = 0 and [b] = Λ ∘ b. Hence:
 (a) if b is C^∞ then [b] is C^∞ (composition with a continuous linear map);
 (b) spt [b] ⊆ spt b (because Λ(0) = 0), and if b has compact support then so has [b];
 (c) [b](x)(e) = b(x)·dx(e) = b(x) for all x, by Step 1;
 (d) [a + b] = [a] + [b] and [c·a] = c·[a] (linearity of Λ);
 (e) if b is C^∞ then D^q[b](x) = Λ ∘ D^q b(x) for every q and x (the q-th derivative of a continuous linear map composed with b), hence ‖D^q[b](x)‖ ≤ ‖Λ‖·‖D^q b(x)‖.
 In particular, for admissible b the form [b] is C^∞ with compact support and spt [b] ⊆ spt b ⊆ U, i.e. [b] ∈ Dⁿ(U).

3. (Definition of u.) Put u(b) := T([b]) if b is admissible and u(b) := 0 otherwise (classical case distinction; the values on non-admissible functions are never used).

4. (Proof of (ii).) For admissible b, ω := [b] ∈ Dⁿ(U) by Step 2, and ω(x)(e) = b(x) for all x by 2(c).

5. (Proof of (i).) Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) and a_ω(x) := ω(x)(e). The evaluation ev_e : α ↦ α(e) is a continuous linear map Λⁿ(ℝⁿ) → ℝ with ev_e(0) = 0, and a_ω = ev_e ∘ ω. Since ω is C^∞ with compact support and spt ω ⊆ U, the function a_ω is C^∞, has compact support and spt a_ω ⊆ spt ω ⊆ U; so a_ω is admissible and u(a_ω) = T([a_ω]). By Step 1, for every x, ω(x) = ω(x)(e)·dx = a_ω(x)·dx = [a_ω](x); hence [a_ω] = ω as elements of Dⁿ(U) (same underlying form), and T(ω) = T([a_ω]) = u(a_ω).

6. (Proof of (iii) and (iv).) Let a, b be admissible and c ∈ ℝ. Then a + b and c·a are admissible (sums and scalar multiples of C^∞ compactly supported functions are C^∞ and compactly supported; spt(a + b) ⊆ spt a ∪ spt b ⊆ U and spt(c·a) ⊆ spt a ⊆ U). By 2(d) and the linearity of T on Dⁿ(U): u(a + b) = T([a + b]) = T([a] + [b]) = T([a]) + T([b]) = u(a) + u(b), and u(c·a) = T([c·a]) = T(c·[a]) = c·T([a]) = c·u(a).

7. (Proof of (v).) Let K, a_k, b be as in (v). A closed subset of the compact set K is compact, so every a_k and b has compact support; as spt a_k, spt b ⊆ K ⊆ U, all of them are admissible, and u(a_k) = T([a_k]), u(b) = T([b]). Put ω_k := [a_k] − [b] = [a_k − b] ∈ Dⁿ(U). Then:
 – spt ω_k ⊆ spt(a_k − b) ⊆ spt a_k ∪ spt b ⊆ K, and spt 0 = ∅ ⊆ K;
 – for every q and x, by 2(e) and the linearity of D^q on C^∞ functions, D^q ω_k(x) = Λ ∘ (D^q a_k(x) − D^q b(x)), so ‖D^q ω_k(x) − D^q 0(x)‖ = ‖D^q ω_k(x)‖ ≤ ‖Λ‖·‖D^q a_k(x) − D^q b(x)‖ (D^q of the zero form is 0). Given δ > 0, uniform convergence gives k₀ with ‖D^q a_k(x) − D^q b(x)‖ < δ/(‖Λ‖ + 1) for all k ≥ k₀ and all x, hence ‖D^q ω_k(x)‖ ≤ ‖Λ‖·δ/(‖Λ‖ + 1) < δ for all k ≥ k₀ and all x. Thus D^q ω_k → 0 uniformly on ℝⁿ, in particular uniformly on K.
 Hence ω_k → 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges (with this K). The continuity axiom of T gives T(ω_k) → 0. By linearity T(ω_k) = T([a_k]) − T([b]) = u(a_k) − u(b), so u(a_k) − u(b) → 0, i.e. u(a_k) → u(b).

8. Steps 4–7 prove (i)–(v) for the function u of Step 3. ∎

Formalization notes (no new mathematics; no import beyond the frozen GMT.Ch06.Submission is needed). (a) Take dx := wedgeCovectors (m + 1) (fun i => EuclideanSpace.proj i) from Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.FormsDuality (already imported by the frozen file): it is a continuous alternating map by construction, and wedgeCovectors_apply_det with EuclideanSpace.coe_proj gives dx v = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => v j i); this avoids proving continuity of the determinant by hand. It helps to `generalize` the family (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) to a variable e first. dx e = 1: show the matrix is 1 (ext; simp [Matrix.one_apply, PiLp.single_apply]) and use Matrix.det_one. α = α e • dx: apply AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det to α.toAlternatingMap and (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).toBasis (its coercion is e, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), evaluate at v, unfold Module.Basis.det_apply, then `congr 2` (the two matrices agree definitionally). (b) Λ := ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ ℝ) dx, with Λ t = t • dx by rfl; the test form [b] is fun x => Λ (b x) with membership proof ⟨⟨Λ.contDiff.comp hb, hcb.comp_left (map_zero Λ)⟩, (tsupport_comp_subset (map_zero Λ) b).trans hsb⟩ in testFormOnSubmodule U (m + 1). (c) Define u by a classical `if h : (ContDiff ℝ _ b ∧ HasCompactSupport b ∧ tsupport b ⊆ U) then T ⟨fun x => Λ (b x), _⟩ else 0` and evaluate it with dite_eq_left; linearity of T is map_add, map_smul, map_sub applied to T.toCurrent. (d) In (i), ev_e is ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Eucl (m + 1)) ℝ e; prove [a_ω] = ω by Subtype.ext and funext. (e) In (v), use ContinuousLinearMap.iteratedFDeriv_comp_left, iteratedFDeriv_sub_apply (ContDiffAt of order q via `.of_le (by simp)`), ContinuousLinearMap.norm_compContinuousMultilinearMap_le, Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff, TendstoUniformly.tendstoUniformlyOn, IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset with isClosed_tsupport, tsupport_sub, then T.continuous' and tendsto_sub_nhds_zero_iff.

subproblems.title: The mollified functional F(f) = u(φ ∗ 1_B f) is linear and L¹(B)-bounded (Step 3 of Simon 2.34)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝⁿ and u : (ℝⁿ → ℝ) → ℝ; call a : ℝⁿ → ℝ admissible if a is C^∞, has compact support and spt a ⊆ U (spt g denotes the closed support of g, the closure of {g ≠ 0}; Lean: tsupport g). Assume (L1) u(a + b) = u(a) + u(b) for admissible a, b; (L2) u(c·a) = c·u(a) for c ∈ ℝ and admissible a; (C) whenever K ⊆ U is compact, a_k (k ∈ ℕ) and b are C^∞ functions ℝⁿ → ℝ with spt a_k ⊆ K for all k and spt b ⊆ K, and D^q a_k → D^q b uniformly on ℝⁿ for every q ∈ ℕ, then u(a_k) → u(b). Let x₀ ∈ ℝⁿ, ρ > 0 and ε > 0 with B̄_{ρ+ε}(x₀) ⊆ U, and put B := B_ρ(x₀). Let φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and spt φ ⊆ B̄_ε(0), such that (Bd) for every q ∈ ℕ there is C_q ∈ ℝ with ‖D^q(φ ∗ g)(x)‖ ≤ C_q ∫|g| dLⁿ for every Lⁿ-integrable g : ℝⁿ → ℝ and every x ∈ ℝⁿ. Here (φ ∗ g)(x) = ∫ φ(t) g(x − t) dLⁿ(t) (Lean: convolution φ g (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) and D^q is the q-th Fréchet derivative. For f : ℝⁿ → ℝ put F(f) := u(φ ∗ (1_B f)), where 1_B f is f on B and 0 off B. Then F(f + g) = F(f) + F(g) and F(c·f) = c·F(f) for all f, g integrable on B and c ∈ ℝ, and there is C ∈ ℝ with |F(f)| ≤ C ∫_B |f| dLⁿ for every f integrable on B.

This child is the first half of Step 3 of that proof, the printed sentence “if a_j → a in L¹(B_ρ(x₀)) … then a_j^(ε) dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ → a^(ε) dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ in Dⁿ(U), and hence T(a_j^(ε) dx) → T(a^(ε) dx). Thus the functional F(a) = T(a^(ε) dx) is a bounded linear functional on L¹(B_ρ(x₀))”, with the scalar functional u in place of a ↦ T(a dx), and with the boundedness made explicit by the contradiction argument given in brackets in Step 3 of the parent proof.
Notation. ℝⁿ = Eucl n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1 is the j-th standard basis vector and e = (e_1,…,e_n); Lⁿ = Lebesgue measure (Lean: volume); spt g = tsupport g (closure of {g ≠ 0}); B_s(x) = ball x s, B̄_s(x) = closedBall x s; D^q g = iteratedFDeriv ℝ q g; D_j g(x) = Dg(x)(e_j) = fderiv ℝ g x (e_j); (f ∗ g)(x) = ∫ f(t) g(x − t) dLⁿ(t) is convolution f g (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume; 1_B f = B.indicator f (f on B, 0 off B); “C^∞” means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞). A function a : ℝⁿ → ℝ is called admissible (for U) if a is C^∞, has compact support and spt a ⊆ U. (L1), (L2), (C) and (Bd) are the hypotheses of the statement, and F(f) := u(φ ∗ 1_B f).

Proof. Throughout, B := B_ρ(x₀) and K := B̄_{ρ+ε}(x₀); K is closed and bounded in ℝⁿ, hence compact, and K ⊆ U by hypothesis. A function g with spt g ⊆ K has compact support (a closed subset of a compact set).

1. (Mollified functions are admissible.) Let f be integrable on B and g := 1_B f. As B is measurable, g is integrable on ℝⁿ, in particular locally integrable. Then:
 (a) φ ∗ g is C^∞ (φ is C^∞ with compact support and g is locally integrable; differentiation under the integral sign);
 (b) {φ ∗ g ≠ 0} ⊆ {φ ≠ 0} + {g ≠ 0} ⊆ B̄_ε(0) + B_ρ(x₀) (spt φ ⊆ B̄_ε(0), and g = 0 off B); if ‖s‖ ≤ ε and ‖t − x₀‖ < ρ then ‖s + t − x₀‖ ≤ ‖s‖ + ‖t − x₀‖ < ρ + ε, so this set lies in K. As K is closed, spt(φ ∗ g) ⊆ K; hence φ ∗ g has compact support and is admissible with spt(φ ∗ g) ⊆ K;
 (c) the convolution integral defining φ ∗ g converges at every point (φ is continuous with compact support and g is locally integrable).

2. (Linearity of F.) Let f, h be integrable on B and c ∈ ℝ. Then 1_B(f + h) = 1_B f + 1_B h and 1_B(c·f) = c·1_B f. By 1(c) the convolution is additive, φ ∗ (1_B f + 1_B h) = φ ∗ 1_B f + φ ∗ 1_B h, and it is homogeneous, φ ∗ (c·1_B f) = c·(φ ∗ 1_B f). The functions φ ∗ 1_B f and φ ∗ 1_B h are admissible by Step 1, so (L1) and (L2) give F(f + h) = F(f) + F(h) and F(c·f) = c·F(f).

3. (u(0) = 0.) The zero function is admissible (C^∞, spt 0 = ∅), so (L2) with c = 0 and a = 0 gives u(0) = u(0·0) = 0·u(0) = 0.

4. (Boundedness, by contradiction.) Suppose that no C ∈ ℝ satisfies |F(f)| ≤ C ∫_B |f| dLⁿ for all f integrable on B. Then for every k ∈ ℕ (taking C = k + 1) there is f_k integrable on B with |F(f_k)| > (k + 1)·∫_B |f_k| dLⁿ. The right-hand side is ≥ 0, so F(f_k) ≠ 0. Put g_k := F(f_k)⁻¹·f_k. Then g_k is integrable on B, F(g_k) = F(f_k)⁻¹·F(f_k) = 1 by Step 2, and
 ∫_B |g_k| dLⁿ = |F(f_k)|⁻¹·∫_B |f_k| dLⁿ ≤ 1/(k + 1)   (because (k + 1)·∫_B |f_k| < |F(f_k)|).
 Let b_k := φ ∗ 1_B g_k. By Step 1 each b_k is C^∞ with spt b_k ⊆ K. Apply (Bd) to the integrable function 1_B g_k, for which ∫ |1_B g_k| dLⁿ = ∫_B |g_k| dLⁿ ≤ 1/(k + 1): for every q and x, ‖D^q b_k(x)‖ ≤ C_q·∫_B |g_k| ≤ max(C_q, 0)/(k + 1). Since max(C_q, 0)/(k + 1) → 0, for every q we get D^q b_k → 0 = D^q 0 uniformly on ℝⁿ, where 0 is the zero function (C^∞, spt 0 = ∅ ⊆ K). By (C), applied with this K, a_k := b_k and b := 0, u(b_k) → u(0) = 0 (Step 3). But u(b_k) = F(g_k) = 1 for every k, and the constant sequence 1 does not converge to 0: a contradiction.
 Hence there is C ∈ ℝ with |F(f)| ≤ C ∫_B |f| dLⁿ for every f integrable on B.
 [This is the bracketed argument of Step 3 of the parent proof — normalize counterexamples so that their L¹(B) norms tend to 0 while F stays away from 0, then contradict sequential continuity — with the normalization by F(f_k) instead of by ∫_B |f_k|, which makes a separate treatment of the case ∫_B |f_k| = 0 unnecessary.]

5. Steps 2 and 4 are the three assertions of the statement. ∎

Source: Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 6, Theorem 2.34 (Constancy Theorem) and its printed proof, pp. 142–143, as expanded in the accepted proof of the parent node root.constancy-a1.local_on_balls-a1 (book n = m + 1; erratum applied there: the garbled printed display (1) reads T(a_ε dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ) = ∫ a θ_ε dLⁿ for a ∈ L¹(B_ρ(x₀)), with a_ε = ϕ_ε ∗ a). This child is Step 4 of that proof: the printed display (2), “∫ D_j a θ_ε dLⁿ = T(dω_j) = ∂T(ω_j) = 0, j = 1,…,n”, and the following conclusion that θ_ε is constant on B_ρ(x₀); the hypothesis u(D_j a) = 0 plays the role of T(dω_j) = ∂T(ω_j) = 0, and a general kernel φ that of ϕ_ε.
Notation. ℝⁿ = Eucl n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1 is the j-th standard basis vector and e = (e_1,…,e_n); Lⁿ = Lebesgue measure (Lean: volume); spt g = tsupport g (closure of {g ≠ 0}); B_s(x) = ball x s, B̄_s(x) = closedBall x s; D^q g = iteratedFDeriv ℝ q g; D_j g(x) = Dg(x)(e_j) = fderiv ℝ g x (e_j); (f ∗ g)(x) = ∫ f(t) g(x − t) dLⁿ(t) is convolution f g (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume; 1_B f = B.indicator f (f on B, 0 off B); “C^∞” means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞). A function a : ℝⁿ → ℝ is called admissible (for U) if a is C^∞, has compact support and spt a ⊆ U.

Proof. Put B := B_ρ(x₀).

1. (Test functions in B.) Let a : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C¹ with compact support and spt a ⊆ B, and let j ∈ {1,…,n}. Put d := D_j a, d(x) = Da(x)(e_j). Then d is continuous (Da is continuous), and spt d ⊆ spt a ⊆ B (the derivative vanishes on the open set where a vanishes identically). So d has compact support, d is integrable on ℝⁿ (continuous with compact support), in particular integrable on B, d = 0 outside B, and 1_B d = d.

2. (φ ∗ a is admissible.) φ ∗ a is C^∞ (φ is C^∞ with compact support; a is continuous, hence locally integrable). Moreover {φ ∗ a ≠ 0} ⊆ {φ ≠ 0} + {a ≠ 0} ⊆ B̄_ε(0) + B_ρ(x₀) ⊆ B̄_{ρ+ε}(x₀) (‖s + t − x₀‖ ≤ ‖s‖ + ‖t − x₀‖ ≤ ε + ρ). Hence spt(φ ∗ a) ⊆ B̄_{ρ+ε}(x₀) ⊆ U, and φ ∗ a has compact support (the convolution of two compactly supported functions). So φ ∗ a is C^∞ with compact support and spt(φ ∗ a) ⊆ U.

3. (The derivative falls on a; fact (M4) of the parent proof.) Since a is C¹ with compact support and φ is locally integrable, φ ∗ a is differentiable at every x with D(φ ∗ a)(x) = (φ ∗ Da)(x), the convolution of φ with the operator-valued function Da (differentiation under the integral sign). Evaluating at e_j (evaluation at a fixed vector commutes with the convolution integral, since Da is continuous with compact support) gives D_j(φ ∗ a)(x) = (φ ∗ d)(x) for every x. Hence the functions D_j(φ ∗ a) and φ ∗ d = φ ∗ (1_B d) coincide.

4. (Printed display (2).) By the hypothesis on u applied to the admissible function φ ∗ a of Step 2, u(D_j(φ ∗ a)) = 0. Using Step 3 and then hypothesis (1) with f := d (integrable on B by Step 1):
 ∫_B d θ dLⁿ = u(φ ∗ (1_B d)) = u(D_j(φ ∗ a)) = 0.
 Since d = 0 outside B, ∫_{ℝⁿ} θ(x)·Da(x)(e_j) dx = ∫_B θ d dLⁿ = ∫_B d θ dLⁿ = 0.
 [Printed form: with ω_j = (−1)^{j−1} a_ε dx¹∧⋯∧dx^{j−1}∧dx^{j+1}∧⋯∧dxⁿ one has dω_j = (D_j a)_ε dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ, and (2) reads ∫ D_j a θ_ε = T(dω_j) = ∂T(ω_j) = 0.]

5. (θ is a.e. constant on B.) θ is measurable and |θ| ≤ M, hence integrable on every compact set (compact sets have finite Lebesgue measure); so θ is locally integrable on ℝⁿ and therefore locally integrable on B. B is open and convex, hence preconnected. Step 4 shows ∫ θ(x)·Da(x)(e_j) dx = 0 for every C¹ compactly supported a with spt a ⊆ B and every j, where e_j = (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ) j. These are exactly the hypotheses of the kernel-checked lemma Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero (module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.DistributionalConstancy of the pinned simongmt package; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only), applied with B in place of U and θ in place of f. It yields c ∈ ℝ with θ(x) = c for Lⁿ-a.e. x ∈ B. [This lemma is exactly the printed argument: for 0 < σ < ρ and a mollifier ϕ_σ (C^∞, ≥ 0, ∫ ϕ_σ = 1, spt ϕ_σ ⊆ B̄_σ(0)) the C^∞ function ϕ_σ ∗ (1_B θ) has zero first derivatives on B_{ρ−σ}(x₀) (apply (2) to a = ϕ_σ(x − ·)), hence is constant there, and letting σ ↓ 0 (Lebesgue differentiation) θ is a.e. constant on B.]

6. (Conclusion.) For every f integrable on B, by (1) and Step 5, u(φ ∗ (1_B f)) = ∫_B f θ dLⁿ = ∫_B f·c dLⁿ = c ∫_B f dLⁿ: the integrands f θ and f·c agree Lⁿ-a.e. on B, and the constant factor comes out of the integral. ∎

Notation. ℝⁿ = Eucl n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1 is the j-th standard basis vector and e = (e_1,…,e_n); Lⁿ = Lebesgue measure (Lean: volume); spt g = tsupport g (closure of {g ≠ 0}); B_s(x) = ball x s, B̄_s(x) = closedBall x s; D^q g = iteratedFDeriv ℝ q g; D_j g(x) = Dg(x)(e_j) = fderiv ℝ g x (e_j); (f ∗ g)(x) = ∫ f(t) g(x − t) dLⁿ(t) is convolution f g (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume; 1_B f = B.indicator f (f on B, 0 off B); “C^∞” means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞). A function a : ℝⁿ → ℝ is called admissible (for U) if a is C^∞, has compact support and spt a ⊆ U. (C) is the continuity hypothesis of the statement.

Proof. Put B := B_ρ(x₀) and K := B̄_R(x₀); K is compact and K ⊆ U.

1. (The representation for smooth b.) Let b be C^∞ with compact support and spt b ⊆ B. Then b is integrable (continuous with compact support), hence integrable on B; 1_B b = b (b vanishes outside spt b ⊆ B); and ∫_B b dLⁿ = ∫ b dLⁿ (b = 0 off B). The hypothesis on c_k with f := b therefore gives u(ψ_k ∗ b) = c_k ∫ b dLⁿ for every k.

2. (ψ_k ∗ b and b have support in K.) For b as in Step 1 and every k: ψ_k ∗ b is C^∞ (b is C^∞ with compact support and ψ_k is continuous, hence locally integrable; the derivatives fall on b). {ψ_k ∗ b ≠ 0} ⊆ {ψ_k ≠ 0} + {b ≠ 0} ⊆ B̄_{r_k}(0) + B_ρ(x₀) ⊆ B̄_{ρ+r_k}(x₀) (‖s + t − x₀‖ ≤ ‖s‖ + ‖t − x₀‖ ≤ r_k + ρ); this ball is closed, so spt(ψ_k ∗ b) ⊆ B̄_{ρ+r_k}(x₀) ⊆ K because ρ + r_k ≤ R. Also spt b ⊆ B_ρ(x₀) ⊆ B̄_{ρ+r_0}(x₀) ⊆ K (as r_0 ≥ 0 and ρ + r_0 ≤ R).

3. (Convergence of u(ψ_k ∗ b).) For b as in Step 1, the convergence hypothesis gives D^q(ψ_k ∗ b) → D^q b uniformly on ℝⁿ for every q; together with Step 2, condition (C) (with this K and a_k := ψ_k ∗ b) gives u(ψ_k ∗ b) → u(b).

4. (The constants converge.) Fix b₀ : ℝⁿ → ℝ, C^∞ with compact support, spt b₀ ⊆ B and ∫ b₀ dLⁿ = 1: the normalized smooth bump function centred at x₀ with inner radius ρ/4 and outer radius ρ/2 (its support is B̄_{ρ/2}(x₀) ⊆ B_ρ(x₀) and its integral is 1). By Step 1, u(ψ_k ∗ b₀) = c_k ∫ b₀ = c_k for every k, and by Step 3, c_k = u(ψ_k ∗ b₀) → u(b₀) =: c₀.

5. (Conclusion.) Let b be C^∞ with compact support and spt b ⊆ B. By Steps 1 and 4, u(ψ_k ∗ b) = c_k ∫ b → c₀ ∫ b; by Step 3, u(ψ_k ∗ b) → u(b). Limits in ℝ are unique, so u(b) = c₀ ∫ b dLⁿ. ∎
